findings.description: When a dialog replaces the box during the paste-settle window, the new clear step reads the old echo above the dialog as a draft. It then sends up to 64 Ctrl-U presses into the dialog (about 10 s), and the CLI still says the box "was cleared". Before this commit nothing was pressed in that case.
findings.body:
**A failed paste under a dialog now sends up to 64 Ctrl-U presses into the dialog, and the CLI then says the box "was cleared"**

When the paste never shows whole, `pasteIntoPane` now calls `clearInputBox` without checking whether a box is still on screen:

```ts
export function pasteIntoPane(pane: SessionPane, message: string): boolean {
  pasteText(pane, message);
  if (awaitPasteLanded(pane, message)) return true;
  clearInputBox(pane);
  return false;
}
```

How `clearInputBox` behaves under a dialog:

- It stops early only when `hasUnsubmittedInput(captureInputBox(pane))` turns false.
- `hasUnsubmittedInput` still goes through `inputBoxText`, which takes the last column-0 `❯` and has no frame check. Only `inputBoxState` got the frame check in this commit.
- So on this commit's own fixture (an echoed `❯ merge t-1 next` above ` ❯ 1. Wait for the limit to reset`), it reads the echo as text every time.
- The loop therefore runs to `CLEAR_KEY_LIMIT` = 64 × `CLEAR_SETTLE_MS` = 150 ms: about 10 s of `C-u` presses into the dialog. It then returns false, and `pasteIntoPane` ignores that result.

The trigger is reachable:

- `tellConductor` only needs a framed, empty box before the paste, and the conductor can be mid-turn with its last prompt echoed above the box.
- A usage-limit or model-fallback selector can replace the box during the at least 5 × 700 ms `awaitPasteLanded` window.
- A dialog appearing is one of the likeliest reasons a paste never shows whole, so this is the main way into the clear step, not a rare edge.

Before this commit, this path pressed nothing. Now it presses keys in a dialog, which is the echo-reads-as-text mistake the same commit fixes for the second Enter (decision 85: "never when a dialog has replaced the box"). `src/cli/index.ts` also tells the operator unconditionally that the box "was cleared", which is false here.

Fix: clear only a box that is still framed. `readInputBox` is in the same module and already runs the frame check. If you take this, also make the CLI's "(and was cleared)" wording conditional or drop it.

findings.description: The change copies the "last column-0 `INPUT_PROMPT` row" search into `inputBoxState`, which already exists in `inputBoxText` (lines 117-122). The two now answer "where is the input box" separately: `inputBoxText` accepts any last column-0 prompt with no frame check, while `inputBoxState` also requires `BOX_BORDER` above it. `hasUnsubmittedInput` and `pasteLanded` still use the unframed version, so the same pane gets different answers depending on the entry point. `inputBoxState` also parses the pane twice, because it calls `hasUnsubmittedInput`. One shared locator that applies the frame rule would keep them from drifting.

Decision 85's Tests paragraph credits `tellConductor` with the runtime mocked for two tests it doesn't have. "Clears the box" is tested on `pasteIntoPane` against the fake tmux in session-runtime.test.ts, and conductor.test.ts mocks `pasteIntoPane` and only asserts that no Enter was pressed. "Reads a dialog under an echoed prompt as no box" is tested on `inputBoxState` in pane-utils.test.ts. The inserted line is also not re-wrapped to the paragraph's width.

The JSDoc on `inputBoxText` still says the input box is the last column-0 `❯` and that it returns undefined when there is no box ("a dialog, a dead pane"). After this change, a dialog under an echoed prompt returns the echo's text, and `inputBoxState` decides whether that row is really the box. Say "undefined when no column-0 `❯` is on screen" and point to `inputBoxState`.

The JSDoc on `BOX_BORDER` still calls it "the box's bottom border", but `inputBoxState` now also uses it as the top border that tells the box from an echo. The comment should say it matches both borders.
